--frozen: uses the lockfile as the source of truth without checking whether it is up to date against pyproject.toml; no re-lock. If pyproject.toml and uv.lock disagree, uv will install what the lock says without error. (Missing lockfile presumably errors; not verified in the fetched text.)

`uv sync` is exact by default: it removes packages in the environment that are not in the lockfile. Use `uv sync --inexact` to keep extraneous packages. `uv run` defaults the opposite (inexact); `uv run --exact` makes it exact.

Recommendation (policy, not sourced fact): In CI, gate with `uv lock --check` or `uv sync --locked`, so a stale lock fails the build. In production deploy/image builds, run `uv sync --locked` (add `--no-dev` and other group flags as appropriate), keeping the default exact sync so the environment matches the lock. Use --frozen only where the lock was already validated in CI and the build context lacks metadata/needs speed (e.g. layered Docker builds), accepting that drift goes undetected. Add --offline with a pre-populated cache/internal index only if network isolation is required. Avoid --inexact in production unless extras are intentionally managed.

## Automatic lock and sync (`--locked`, `--frozen`)

- **`--locked`:** "If the lockfile is not up-to-date, uv will raise an error instead of updating the lockfile."
- **`--frozen`:** The docs say to use it "To use the lockfile without checking if it is up-to-date."

## Checking the lockfile (freshness checks)

- The docs say uv checks "if it matches the project metadata" when considering whether the lockfile is up-to-date.
- Adding a dependency makes the lockfile outdated. Changing a constraint so the locked version is excluded also makes it outdated. If the locked version is still included, the lockfile remains up-to-date.
- `uv lock --check` tests freshness, and the docs say it is "equivalent to the `--locked` flag for other commands."
- uv does not treat the lockfile as outdated when new package versions are released: "uv will not consider lockfiles outdated when new versions of packages are released."

## Exact vs. inexact syncing (`--inexact`)

- `uv sync` defaults to exact syncing: "exact" syncing by default, which means it will remove any packages that are not present in the lockfile.
- To keep extraneous packages, use the `--inexact` flag.
- `uv run` defaults to inexact syncing, which installs required packages without removing extras.
- To get exact syncing with `uv run`, use `--exact`.

## Network and offline behavior

The page does not cover network or offline behavior. It has no guidance on running lock or sync without network access, and it does not describe how `--locked` or `--frozen` interact with network availability.
